newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-MIKE TYSON'S CAREER MAY BE OVER.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-MIKE TYSON'S CAREER MAY BE OVER.

text.p: He called himself "the baddest man on the planet" and on Wednesday the reality behind that image finally did him in.

Mike Tyson, a former juvenile deliquent, mugger, alleged wife beater, convicted rapist and world-class street brawler was thrown out of boxing on Wednesday for doing the one thing a mother always warns her child not to do -- bite.

The one-time king of the ring, the up-from-dirt Brooklyn slum kid who always seemed to revel in the pain of others, had his license to box revoked by the Nevada State Athletic Commission for biting Evander Holyfield's ears in a bout watched by much of the cable-wired planet on June 28.

Holyfield, a devout Christian, had no comment but much of the fight world was quick to imagine the end of an extraordinarily brutal boxing career that reached a peak 11 years and one rape conviction ago when Tyson at age 20 became the youngest ever heavyweight champion.

Bert Sugar, the former editor of Ring magazine and fight historian, predicted that the curtain had finally come down on Tyson's career. "I think we have seen the last of Mike Tyson," he said in a CNN interview.

Tyson's own lawyer, Oscar Goodman, tried to stop the commission from throwing his client out of boxing, arguing that in 13 years of fighting, "He brought nothing but credit to the boxing profession ... he was a gentleman, he remains a gentleman today. He maintains his dignity today."
Goodman added that Tyson always shook the hand of his opponent after the fight was over, even when he lost.
And he only bit the ears of an opponent once -- June 28, 1997 when he fought Holyfield in a futile effort to regain the championship he had last November.
Few people other than his paid defender have ever called Tyson a gentleman.
Former world heavyweight champion Larry Holmes said before they fought in 1988 that Tyson would end up either dead or in prison within five years.
"He's going down in history as an SOB. If he do happen to win the fight, down the line he'll destroy himself," said Holmes, who was knocked out in the fourth round.
Tyson may have thrown thousands of punches but according to his ex-friend Jose Torres, the one punch he remembered best was the one he used to belt his former wife, actress Robin Givens.
"I went bam and she flew backward, hitting every ----- wall in the apartment," Tyson said, according to Torres, a former boxing champion.

Tyson's career may have finally ended Friday, but it also came to an abrupt halt on March 26, 1992 when he was sentenced to six years in jail for the rape of Desiree Washington, a 19-year-old black beauty contestant from Rhode Island.
Tyson served three years with time off for good behaviour, saying he studied philosophy in prison, converted to Islam and had become a changed man.
Out of jail, he immediately resumed his career and regained one championship title in March 1996 when he beat Briton Frank Bruno and another later that year when he knocked out Bruce Seldon.
But he lost the WBA title he regained from Seldon when he he fought Holyfield last November. He had hoped the June 28 rematch would make him king of boxing once again.
Instead of renewed glory, Tyson was criticised by everyone from President Clinton on down for biting his opponent in a sport where it is considered okay to bash a man's head in.
At first he tried to defend himself saying Holyfield had head-butted him and he was trying to get even.
But he later admitted he had "snapped" and apologised to Holyfield.
Tyson can reapply for his license in a year but no one can say with any certainty whether he will ever get it back or whether he will ever step into a ring again.
